note: Western Australia has no destinations or spots in the app yet: every destination below is a proposal for the owner, not added. Placed: every skeptic/verdict keep (83), two of them merged into another kept spot. Reviews are listed, not placed. Coordinates marked in needs_research are hints only; every pin is resolved with resolve-pin.py in the next stage, and hours, cost and ticketUrl go to Pipeline C research. Names follow the judges' notes (Black Diamond Lake, King Jarrah).

destinations.name: Margaret River Region
destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Margaret River, Western Australia (the town, the region's visitor hub and the middle of its spots between the two capes)

name_evidence.source: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA): travel stories "Bays, Beaches and Sting Rays in the Margaret River Region" and the page "Margaret River region beaches"; margaretriver.com, the regional board (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association); Wikivoyage "Margaret River": "now the common term for the region between the capes"

destinations.shape_note: The named region rather than the inland town: its draws (caves, lighthouses, surf beaches, wineries, karri forest) run 95 km from Cape Naturaliste to Cape Leeuwin, and the town is one stop in the middle. Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park covers the same strip; under "No overlapping destinations" the region visitors plan around is the destination and the park is its spot (a park as a spot of a region, not of another park). Busselton, inside the span on its north-east edge, is proposed as its own city destination (a separate base, as Blenheim is to Marlborough); the alternative is to fold Busselton's four spots in here, since the regional board brands Busselton as part of the Margaret River Region.
destinations.action: new-destination (proposal for the owner; not added)

name_evidence.source: southernforestsandvalleys.com, the regional tourism organisation ("Southern Forests & Valleys"); westernaustralia.com travel story "Feasting Al Fresco in the Southern Forests" and its "Southern Forests Wine Region" page (Pemberton and Manjimup)

destinations.shape_note: The named region rather than Pemberton alone: Pemberton's draws are the climbing trees, falls and parks around it, and Manjimup (25 km) and Northcliffe (21 km) share them. No park here has four kept spots of its own (Warren 1, D'Entrecasteaux 1 here, Shannon 0), so the parks are spots of the region. Wikivoyage has no "Southern Forests" page (it has Pemberton), so the name rests on the regional brand and Tourism WA; the fallback is "Pemberton" with the same spots.
destinations.action: new-destination (proposal for the owner; not added)

entries.name: D'Entrecasteaux National Park

entries.bio: Wild coastal park between Augusta and Walpole, with Point D'Entrecasteaux, Windy Harbour and the Black Point basalt columns.
entries.reason: Inside the Southern Forests span and reached from Pemberton, Manjimup or Northcliffe. Long linear park placed at its main 2WD visitor point, Point D'Entrecasteaux and Windy Harbour, reached from Northcliffe (44 km from Pemberton, inside the 45 km radius). Its far-east Mandalay Beach is reached from Walpole and stands alone.

entries.name: Big Brook Dam
entries.coordinates_source: needs the day-use area point (the candidate point is the reservoir centroid, in the water)
entries.bio: Forest dam near Pemberton with a 3.5 km sealed loop walk, a small beach and picnic areas.
entries.reason: Inside the Southern Forests span and reached from Pemberton, Manjimup or Northcliffe.

entries.name: Shannon National Park
entries.coordinates_source: needs the park's visitor point (the Shannon day-use area or campground) from OSM or DBCA, not the Wikipedia centroid
entries.bio: Old-growth karri park east of Northcliffe, with the Great Forest Trees Drive, Snake Gully Lookout and Big Tree Grove.
entries.reason: Inside the Southern Forests span and reached from Pemberton, Manjimup or Northcliffe. Its centroid is 35 km from Pemberton, inside the 45 km radius; reached on the drive from Manjimup or Pemberton to Walpole.

entries.name: Manjimup Heritage Park
entries.coordinates_source: Commons geotag median (LOW: resolve to OSM)
entries.bio: Heritage park in Manjimup with a timber museum, an Age of Steam museum, a historic hamlet and an electricity museum.
entries.candidate_name: Manjimup Heritage Park & Power Up Museum
entries.reason: Inside the Southern Forests span and reached from Pemberton, Manjimup or Northcliffe.

entries.name: King Jarrah
entries.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=picnic_site "King Jarrah" (via Photon; not the Dwellingup trail of the same name)
entries.bio: Jarrah about 500 years old and 45 m tall, spared by sleeper cutters, on a short sealed path near Manjimup.
entries.reason: Inside the Southern Forests span and reached from Pemberton, Manjimup or Northcliffe. Named "King Jarrah", the sources' name, as the judge directed.

entries.name: Manjimup
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Manjimup, Western Australia (resolve to OSM place=town)
entries.bio: Regional hub of the Southern Forests farming district, with its heritage park and King Jarrah on the town's edge.
entries.reason: Inside the Southern Forests span and reached from Pemberton, Manjimup or Northcliffe. Kept as the region's second town (COVERAGE: sizable settlements and hubs); the skeptic noted its best sights are separate spots, so it sits low in the order. If the owner reads it as a wrapper for its heritage park, fold it into the description.

entries.name: Understory Art and Nature Trail
entries.coordinates_source: OSM highway=footway "Understory, Art In Nature Trail" (via Photon: one segment; pin the loop's midpoint in research)
entries.bio: Sculpture trail of 1.2 km through Northcliffe's forest with dozens of artworks, entered from the visitor centre.
entries.reason: Inside the Southern Forests span and reached from Pemberton, Manjimup or Northcliffe. In Northcliffe (the candidate note's "near Dunsborough" was wrong); 21 km from Pemberton. Carries Northcliffe (review) if the owner rejects the village.

entries.name: Blackwood River
entries.coordinates_source: long river: pin its main visitor access point (the Nannup town reach or Wrights Bridge, per the skeptic), not the Wikipedia point near Augusta
entries.bio: The South West's main paddling river, with canoe sections and swimming pools between Bridgetown and Nannup.
entries.reason: Inside the Blackwood Valley span and reached along the valley road between Nannup, Balingup and Bridgetown. A long linear feature placed where visitors reach it (COVERAGE "How far a spot reaches"). Carries Blackwood River National Park (review) if the owner rejects it.

entries.name: Bridgetown
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Bridgetown, Western Australia (resolve to OSM place=town)
entries.bio: Blackwood River town of historic buildings and galleries, with an art trail through its streets.
entries.reason: Inside the Blackwood Valley span and reached along the valley road between Nannup, Balingup and Bridgetown. Its Blues festival is an event and goes in the description, not a spot.

entries.name: Nannup
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Nannup, Western Australia (rounded: resolve to OSM place=town)
entries.bio: Small forest town on the Blackwood River with a heritage trail of 51 sites, galleries and the Tank 7 lookout.
entries.reason: Inside the Blackwood Valley span and reached along the valley road between Nannup, Balingup and Bridgetown.

entries.name: Balingup
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Balingup (resolve to OSM place=village)
entries.bio: Small Blackwood valley village of artisans' shops and scarecrows on one of the state's best-known scenic drives.
entries.reason: Inside the Blackwood Valley span and reached along the valley road between Nannup, Balingup and Bridgetown. Kept beside Golden Valley Tree Park: the main street's artisans are a draw the tree park does not cover.

entries.name: Golden Valley Tree Park
entries.coordinates_source: OSM leisure=park "Golden Valley Tree Park" (via Photon: the park area; pin its entrance in research). The candidate's Commons point was at the Gloucester Tree and is not used.
entries.bio: Arboretum of 60 ha south of Balingup with more than 500 tree species and walk trails, best in autumn colour.
entries.reason: Inside the Blackwood Valley span and reached along the valley road between Nannup, Balingup and Bridgetown.

entries.name: Bibbulmun Track
entries.coordinates_source: pin at the midpoint of the whole OSM route=hiking relation (resolve-pin.py), per the run-wide decision
entries.bio: Long-distance walking track of about 1,000 km from Kalamunda in the Perth Hills to Albany through the southern forests.
entries.reason: Run-wide decision: placed once, here, at the midpoint of the whole route. A 1,000 km track crosses several destinations and belongs to none (COVERAGE: a long linear feature is not a spot of whatever it touches). If its midpoint falls within 40 km of a proposed destination's centre, it still stands alone for this reason.

entries.name: Munda Biddi Trail
entries.coordinates_source: pin at the midpoint of the whole OSM route (resolve-pin.py), per the run-wide decision
entries.bio: Off-road cycling trail of about 1,000 km from Mundaring to Albany, through jarrah and karri forest and the trail towns.
entries.reason: Run-wide decision: placed once, here, at the midpoint of the whole route; a 1,000 km trail belongs to no one destination.

entries.name: Ferguson Valley
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Ferguson, Western Australia (the locality point; rounded: resolve to the valley's visitor point)
entries.bio: Inland valley of vineyards, microbreweries and orchards in the hills between Donnybrook and Harvey.
entries.reason: An inland food-and-wine valley with its own drive, reached as a day out from Bunbury or Collie; two kept places (with Gnomesville) are too few for a destination.

why_not_spot_of.bunbury: Inland hill valley 23 km from Bunbury: visitors drive its own wine-and-produce loop, and Bunbury's span (15 km, its five city spots within 3 km) would have to balloon to 45 km to hold it.
why_not_spot_of.collie: On the far side of Wellington National Park from Collie (30 km); visitors reach it from Bunbury and Dardanup, not Collie.

entries.name: Gnomesville
entries.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=attraction "Gnomesville" (via Photon; the candidate point was the Wellington Mill locality)
entries.bio: Roadside village of thousands of garden gnomes at the Wellington Mill roundabout in the Ferguson Valley.
entries.reason: Quirky roadside icon on the Ferguson Valley drive; partly damaged by a November 2024 flood and under restoration (confirm in research).

why_not_spot_of.bunbury: 30 km inland of Bunbury on the Ferguson Valley drive; outside Bunbury's city span.
why_not_spot_of.collie: 25 km from Collie but reached from the Ferguson Valley side (Wellington Mill road from Dardanup), not from Collie; Collie's span is 30 km (22.5 km radius).

entries.name: Harvey
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Harvey, Western Australia (rounded: resolve to OSM place=town)
entries.bio: Farming town on the Harvey River known for its cheese, craft beer, wine and orange juice, and its Noongar and Italian heritage.
entries.reason: A town on the South Western Highway with its own Tourism WA section; with the Boola Bidi Dreaming Centre it makes two kept places, too few for a destination. Kept beside Boola Bidi: the source's draws (cheese, beer, wine, juice) are the town's own, not the cultural centre's.

why_not_spot_of.bunbury: 36 km north of Bunbury, a separate highway town that visitors stop in on their own; Bunbury's span would balloon.
why_not_spot_of.collie: 40 km away over the scarp; not reached from Collie.

entries.name: Boola Bidi Dreaming Centre
entries.coordinates_source: none in the candidate; Photon found no match: resolve from OSM (Stirling Gardens precinct, Harvey)
entries.bio: Noongar cultural centre in Harvey with Elder-guided walks and a 900 m knowledge path along the Harvey River.
entries.reason: A cultural centre in Harvey, which is not a destination (see Harvey).

why_not_spot_of.bunbury: In Harvey, 36 km north of Bunbury (see Harvey).
why_not_spot_of.collie: In Harvey, about 40 km from Collie (see Harvey).

entries.name: Donnybrook
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Donnybrook, Western Australia (rounded: resolve to OSM place=town)
entries.bio: Apple-growing town on the South Western Highway with heritage buildings and a large free-entry fun park.
entries.reason: A highway town between the Geographe coast and the Blackwood valley; no destination's span reaches it.

why_not_spot_of.bunbury: 33 km inland on the highway; a separate town, outside a city span.
why_not_spot_of.collie: 39 km south-west of Collie, not reached from it.
why_not_spot_of.blackwood-valley: 39 km from the valley centre, on the Geographe side (Tourism WA lists it on its Bunbury Geographe page, not the Blackwood Valley); the span would have to grow to 52 km.

entries.name: Peppermint Grove Beach
entries.coordinates_source: needs the OSM natural=beach or the lookout (the candidate point is the Wikipedia locality, rounded)
entries.bio: Geographe Bay swimming beach near Capel with a beach park, a lookout up about 120 steps and the Capel River mouth.
entries.reason: A holiday settlement's beach in the Shire of Capel, between Bunbury and Busselton.

why_not_spot_of.busselton: 21 km from Busselton, just outside its 26 km span (19.5 km radius); the beach belongs to Capel's holiday settlement and its source is the Bunbury Geographe board's Capel page, so it is not a Busselton spot.
why_not_spot_of.bunbury: 24 km from Bunbury, outside its 15 km city span.

entries.name: Mandalay Beach
entries.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=viewpoint "Mandalay Beach" (via Photon; confirm with resolve-pin.py)
entries.bio: Remote beach in D'Entrecasteaux National Park with whale-watching platforms and the 1911 Mandalay wreck at low tide.
entries.reason: Moved here at reconciliation. Reached from Walpole (wa-great-southern), 77 km from the Southern Forests centre; no wa-south-west destination is near. If wa-great-southern proposes a Walpole or Walpole-Nornalup destination whose span reaches it, it becomes that destination's spot.

entries.name: Fernhook Falls
entries.coordinates_source: OSM waterway=waterfall "Fernhook Falls" (via Photon; confirm with resolve-pin.py)
entries.bio: Deep River cascades over granite into Rowell's Pool in the Walpole forests, with walk trails and boardwalks.
entries.reason: Moved here at reconciliation. 66 km from the Southern Forests centre and reached from Walpole (wa-great-southern); standalone unless a Walpole destination there takes it.

entries.name: Mount Frankland National Park
entries.coordinates_source: needs the Mount Frankland Wilderness Lookout car park (Towerman's Hut) from OSM or DBCA, not the park centroid
entries.bio: Granite peak in the Walpole Wilderness with a summit walk to a lookout over karri and tingle forest.
entries.reason: Moved here at reconciliation. A small park (the judge: a standalone spot, not a destination); reached from Walpole (wa-great-southern), about 75 km from Pemberton. Standalone unless a Walpole destination there takes it.

entries.name: Busselton
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Busselton
entries.reason: The kept town is the base of a proposed destination of the same name (see destinations[]); it is not also listed as its own spot (no destination is a spot of itself).

entries.name: Bunbury
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Bunbury, Western Australia
entries.reason: The kept town is the base of a proposed destination of the same name (see destinations[]); it is not also listed as its own spot (no destination is a spot of itself).

entries.name: Collie
entries.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Collie, Western Australia (needs an OSM place=town point)
entries.reason: The kept town is the base of a proposed destination of the same name (see destinations[]); it is not also listed as its own spot (no destination is a spot of itself).

merged.name: Yallingup
merged.reason: Judge and skeptic: the beach is the village's draw (Ngilgi Cave, Canal Rocks, Injidup and Smiths Beach are their own spots); listing the village beside its beach is a wrapper. The village goes in the destination description.

merged.name: Meelup Regional Park
merged.reason: Both judges: the park and its beach overlap; keep one. The beach is where visitors go; Eagle Bay and Bunker Bay, inside the park, are their own spots, and the park's coastal trail goes in Meelup Beach's bio.

reviews.name: Boyup Brook
reviews.reason: Re-looked: only southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) lists it, with generic text ('natural wonders, local artisans, local produce'); no named sight.
reviews.skeptic_objection: Against: one counted source and nothing specific to see or do (brief: a town with nothing a source names is reject or review). For: a listed town of the regional board, gateway for country-music events (events do not count).
reviews.if_approved: If approved: standalone (east of the Blackwood Valley span).

reviews.name: Northcliffe
reviews.reason: Re-looked: southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) town page and itinerary name the Understory Art & Nature Walk, the Pioneer Museum, Mount Chudalup and Windy Harbour nearby.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: gateway to D'Entrecasteaux NP and Windy Harbour with a named art trail and museum. Against: one counted source, and its named draws (Understory, Mount Chudalup) are separate candidates, so the town may be a wrapper.
reviews.if_approved: If approved: a Southern Forests spot; otherwise carried by the Understory trail and D'Entrecasteaux NP.

reviews.name: Australind
reviews.reason: Re-looked: harveyregion.com.au (Shire of Harvey tourism) Australind page names the Australind Jetty, the Leschenault Waterways Eco Museum, the estuary crabbing and the heritage trail.
reviews.skeptic_objection: Against: one local-government tourism source; a residential satellite of Bunbury ('Australia's fastest growing regional location') with cafes and a big pub; a traveller from elsewhere rarely goes out of their way for it. For: estuary jetty and eco museum.
reviews.if_approved: If approved: standalone or a Bunbury spot (8 km north on the Leschenault Inlet; would need Bunbury's span widened to 22 km).

reviews.name: Prevelly
reviews.reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Prevelly & Gnarabup' town page names the beaches, Margaret River Mouth, St John the Theologian Church, the Prevelly Sculpture Loop Walk and Surfers Point.
reviews.skeptic_objection: Against: its headline draw is Surfers Point (kept separately), so the village is likely a wrapper or near-duplicate (COVERAGE: never list a town beside its own attraction). For: a named surf village with its own beaches and river mouth.
reviews.if_approved: If approved: a Margaret River Region spot; otherwise carried by Surfers Point and Gnarabup Beach.

reviews.name: St Mary's Church Busselton
reviews.reason: Church rule: Wikivoyage Busselton singles it out (built 1844-45, believed the oldest stone church in WA, graveyard with graves from 1841) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) page says visitors can wander the graveyard and read the settlers' tombstones.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: a landmark guides single out, with a graveyard to explore. Against: the board files it under 'local services', it is a working parish church mostly seen from outside, and the visit is about 15 minutes.
reviews.if_approved: A Busselton spot.

reviews.name: Koombana Beach
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Bunbury See names it (protected beach on Koombana Bay where wild dolphins come close to shore); westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Bunbury text names Koombana Bay and shoreline dolphins.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: wild dolphins at the beach. Against: Wikivoyage calls it 'a modest beach', and the dolphin interaction zone and visitor facilities are the Dolphin Discovery Centre on the same beach, so it is a near-duplicate of that spot.
reviews.if_approved: Skeptic: near-duplicate of the Dolphin Discovery Centre (bunbury-1); if approved, a Bunbury spot.

reviews.name: Cape Leeuwin
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Margaret River 'See' names Cape Leeuwin; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Edge of the world: the great Cape Leeuwin' (where two oceans meet, whales). Strong name (16k views).
reviews.skeptic_objection: Not a separate place from Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse: visitors reach the cape at the lighthouse precinct (ticketed grounds, interpretive centre), which is listed separately by Wikivoyage and the board. Keep as ONE spot (the lighthouse, with 'where two oceans meet' in its bio) rather than both; review only to decide which name carries it.
reviews.if_approved: Skeptic: one place with Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse (margaret-river-region-1); if approved, it is carried by the lighthouse, not added.

reviews.name: Cape Naturaliste
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Leeuwin-Naturaliste NP and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Cape Naturaliste' scenic-spot page (boardwalks, Whale Lookout walk, Cape Naturaliste loop, track to Sugarloaf Rock).
reviews.skeptic_objection: Shares its car park and precinct with Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse, listed separately; the walks are short sections of the Cape to Cape Track. Keep as one with the lighthouse unless the owner wants the headland walks as their own spot.
reviews.if_approved: Skeptic: one place with Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse (margaret-river-region-9); if approved, carried by the lighthouse unless the owner wants the headland walks as their own spot.

reviews.name: Cape Mentelle Vineyards
reviews.reason: Board listing (australiassouthwest.com) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) winery page: founding winery (1970), twice Jimmy Watson trophy winner, cellar door daily, vineyard tours.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: a founding estate a board names. Against: a cellar door like dozens of others, with no visitor attraction beyond tasting; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination in its own right.
reviews.if_approved: A Margaret River Region spot.

reviews.name: Voyager Estate
reviews.reason: Board listing (australiassouthwest.com) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) page: family estate in the Stevens Valley with a wine room, private tours and an award-winning restaurant (Regional Restaurant of the Year 2025).
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: a well-known estate with tours. Against: tastings and dining only; no source read singles it out as a destination beyond the cellar door (brief winery rule).
reviews.if_approved: A Margaret River Region spot.

reviews.name: Cullen Wines
reviews.reason: Re-looked: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Margaret River page names Cullen among the heritage winemakers; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) page (the only biodynamic, carbon-positive winery in the region, wine room open daily).
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: two counted sources, a pioneer estate. Against: a cellar door and restaurant like many others; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination.
reviews.if_approved: A Margaret River Region spot.

reviews.name: Wadandi Track
reviews.reason: Rule 1: the Shire of Augusta Margaret River (managing authority) trail page names it: a walk/cycle rail trail on the former Busselton–Flinders Bay railway, 46 km open in two sections (Busselton Jetty–Carbunup River, Cowaramup–Sebbes Road), being completed to 109 km by 2028. Rule 2 met (walk or ride it).
reviews.skeptic_objection: Only one counted source and that is a council page, not a tourism or guide listing; the trail is incomplete until 2028 and the note placed it 'around Augusta', whereas the open sections are Busselton and Cowaramup; may be better added once finished. Case for: state-funded flagship trail the region is promoting.
reviews.if_approved: If approved: a Margaret River Region or Busselton spot at its route midpoint; incomplete until 2028.

reviews.name: Gloucester National Park
reviews.reason: DBCA page: karri forest walks (Gloucester Tree–Cascades 12 km, 10 km loop, Pemberton town link), mountain biking, the Cascades rapids on Lefroy Brook, Aerial Adventure Pemberton. More than the tree alone.
reviews.skeptic_objection: Near-duplicate of the Gloucester Tree, which is what visitors come for and which sits in it; one counted source (the agency's own page). Keep only if the Cascades/trails are not carried by the tree spot.
reviews.if_approved: If approved: a spot of Southern Forests, pinned at the Cascades, not the Gloucester Tree.

reviews.name: Blackwood River National Park
reviews.reason: DBCA page: canoeing, swimming and fishing on WA's longest continuously flowing river, Sues Bridge and Chapman Pool day-use areas and campgrounds; free entry. The board also lists 'Blackwood River'.
reviews.skeptic_objection: One counted source; the park is a string of river campgrounds rather than a single draw, and paddling the Blackwood is equally done from Nannup or Augusta; may be better as 'Blackwood River' with its access point.
reviews.if_approved: If approved: a Blackwood Valley spot or standalone, pinned at Sues Bridge; otherwise carried by Blackwood River.

reviews.name: Lake Muir National Park
reviews.reason: The candidate park has no DBCA page, but the visitor point beside it does: DBCA's Lake Muir Observatory page (110 m boardwalk through the wetlands to a raised bird hide, picnic shelter, toilets; 'a popular rest stop on the Muir Highway'), also listed by Southern Forests and Valleys. If added, name it Lake Muir Observatory (it is in Lake Muir Nature Reserve, just north of the national park).
reviews.skeptic_objection: A highway rest stop with a 15-30 minute boardwalk; the lake can be a dry bed in summer. Only the agency page plus a local tourism listing.
reviews.if_approved: If approved, name it Lake Muir Observatory (DBCA site, in Lake Muir Nature Reserve); standalone (beyond the Southern Forests span on the Muir Highway).

reviews.name: Harris Dam
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Collie (See): picnic lawns below the dam wall and a walk trail to the top for the view.
reviews.skeptic_objection: One counted source; Wikivoyage itself says 'look is all you can do' (no water activities): a picnic area by a water-supply dam, mostly local use.
reviews.if_approved: A Collie spot (inside its 30 km span, reached from the town).

reviews.name: Glen Mervyn Dam
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Collie (See): a crescent-shaped dam for water skiing, boating and camping, with a bushland walk.
reviews.skeptic_objection: One counted source; a local boating and camping reservoir that visitors from elsewhere rarely travel for.
reviews.if_approved: A Collie spot (inside its 30 km span, reached from the town).

reviews.name: Minninup Pool
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Collie (See): a wide section of the Collie River 3 km south of town for swimming and canoeing; the Shire tests its water with Black Diamond and Stockton.
reviews.skeptic_objection: One counted source; a local swimming hole, and Collie already has stronger swimming spots (Black Diamond, Stockton Lake, Honeymoon Pool).
reviews.if_approved: A Collie spot (inside its 30 km span, reached from the town).

reviews.name: Collie River Walk
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Collie (Do/Hike): a 9 km walk following the Collie River through town.
reviews.skeptic_objection: One line in one source; a town riverside path, more a local amenity than a draw from elsewhere.
reviews.if_approved: A Collie spot (inside its 30 km span, reached from the town).

reviews.name: Collie Railway Museum
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Collie (Museums): reconstructed railway station with railway items and the rediscovered Welsh train drawings, open 9-4 daily, by donation. Open to the public with something to see.
reviews.skeptic_objection: One counted source and a small volunteer museum; a 30-minute stop only if passing through Collie.
reviews.if_approved: A Collie spot (inside its 30 km span, reached from the town).

reviews.name: Coalfields Museum
reviews.reason: Wikivoyage Collie (Museums): mining, timber, farming and social history, open 10-3 daily, $5.
reviews.skeptic_objection: One counted source; a small local-history museum; Collie's coal heritage is its one distinct theme.
reviews.if_approved: A Collie spot (inside its 30 km span, reached from the town).

reviews.name: Aerial Adventure Pemberton
reviews.reason: a permanent high-ropes and zipline park (40 min to 2.5 h courses, ages 4+) in karri forest beside the Gloucester Tree; named by the regional board, the Pemberton Visitor Centre and margaretriver.com
reviews.skeptic_objection: Against: it is an operator's activity course inside Gloucester National Park, next to the Gloucester Tree (risk of being part of that larger spot); paid, booked activity; closes for a winter break. For: a fixed permanent venue, like an amusement park, that visitors travel to Pemberton for.
reviews.if_approved: If approved: a Southern Forests spot, moved 25 m clear of the Gloucester Tree pin.

reviews.name: Nannup Lavender Farm and Campground
reviews.reason: lavender farm near Nannup with fields to walk and pick in (full flower Dec-Jan), a seasonal private garden, tearooms and shop; named by the regional board and Southern Forests and Valleys
reviews.skeptic_objection: Against: mostly a café, gift shop and campground with only seasonal flowering and garden; one-hour stop only if nearby anyway. For: a recognisable farm-gate attraction two regional tourism sources list.
reviews.if_approved: A Blackwood Valley spot.

reviews.name: Origins Market
reviews.reason: Busselton indoor market building with 50-80 makers and producers under one roof; Australia's South West listing and margaretriver.com (which lists an Origins Market Busselton tour). A permanent market hall is allowed by 'What qualifies' 4 if it trades most days.
reviews.skeptic_objection: Trading days unconfirmed (may be only a few days a week, which fails rule 4); it is essentially a food hall and shops (rule 2). Keep only if it trades daily like a market hall.
reviews.if_approved: A Busselton spot.

reviews.name: A Maze'n Margaret River
reviews.reason: Hedge maze and botanical gardens near Margaret River, a permanent paid family attraction for an hour or more ('What qualifies' 2); Australia's South West listing (counted); Wikivoyage Margaret River mentions 'one of the three mazes' without naming it.
reviews.skeptic_objection: Only one counted source names it; a family amusement stop that two other mazes in the area duplicate in kind (Yallingup Maze). Marginal: friend test passes only for families.
reviews.if_approved: A Margaret River Region spot.

reviews.name: Torpedo Rocks
reviews.reason: Granite outcrops and lookout above Yallingup on the Torpedo Trail (3 km loop) and Cape to Cape Track; Trails WA (opened) names the Torpedo Rock car park and lookout. Re-look found one counted source.
reviews.skeptic_objection: Part of a larger walk (Torpedo Trail / Cape to Cape) and a short lookout; one source; could be folded into Yallingup or the Cape to Cape spot ('What qualifies' 3).
reviews.if_approved: A Margaret River Region spot.

duplicates_elsewhere.name: Bibbulmun Track
duplicates_elsewhere.note: Run-wide decision: placed once in wa-south-west at the whole route's midpoint; the other regions must not place it.

duplicates_elsewhere.name: Cape to Cape Track
duplicates_elsewhere.note: Placed in wa-south-west per the run-wide decision.

cross_region_notes: Mandalay Beach, Fernhook Falls and Mount Frankland National Park lie in wa-south-west but are reached from Walpole; wa-great-southern kept Walpole and Walpole-Nornalup National Park. If that region proposes a Walpole destination whose span reaches them, move these three under it (their ids stay).
